args.name: Build a simple shared rain shelter
args.function: Develop a learnable, reusable way to construct a small shelter from obtainable local materials, with an accessible resting area for myself and others.
args.conditions: I am outdoors on ordinary soil. Current health is 100; initial energy is 40. Nearby observations include fallen branches, birch bark, and stone, but their construction properties have not been tested. No shelter or construction mastery is established.
args.inputs: Potential local branches, bark, or stone only if suitable; quantities, tools, site requirements, and method are unknown. Do not assume possession of materials.
args.costs: Unknown material, learning, labor, and maintenance costs; specify a minimal feasible method and prerequisites.
args.effects: A physically constructed, accessible shelter that reduces actual rain exposure if the design and materials support that effect. Specify limitations and a way to test its protection; requesting it alone creates nothing.

args.name: Cultivate meadow roots
args.function: Provide a learnable, evidence-based way to plant or tend meadow roots so a finite food source can be replenished.
args.conditions: A meadow-root patch is visible near (10.1,12). Roots are known to provide 14 nutrition with zero toxicity. Growing requirements and replenishment behavior are unknown.
args.inputs: Potentially real roots, suitable ground, and tending work; exact required inputs need determination.
args.costs: Unknown; require actual time, materials, and any necessary learning rather than instant food or mastery.
args.effects: Enable a practical cultivation trial with observable progress and eventual harvest only if real growing conditions are met; disclose requirements and failure conditions.

candidates.function: Build a low single-person braced lean-to with a sloping bark roof from owned branches, vines and bark at a clear site; inspect, repair or dismantle it, or resume or cancel unfinished work.
candidates.costs: Study: 4 rounds. Start: x, y, orientation (degrees; 0 points the low roof edge toward increasing x, where wind comes from) and materials as exact owned, untreated whole units totalling 13 branch, 4 vine and 6 bark; stand within reach of a 2 m x 2 m footprint of ordinary dry soil that is inside the world, unobstructed and unoccupied. Twelve paid increments, one round and 1 energy each: 2 posts, 3 ridge and braces, 3 ribs and binding, 3 roofing courses, 1 final check; start pays the first and the same action continues each round. Resume pays the next increment of the unfinished work; cancel takes one round and no energy. Inspect: target in reach, one round, 0.2 energy. Repair (builder only): target, increment 1-11 and the exact replacement units of that increment, one round, 1 energy. Dismantle (builder only): target, one round and 1 energy per stage, removing the last installed stage. Gathering, travel and probe tests are separate actions with their own costs.
candidates.effects: Reserved materials stay carried and owned until each paid increment moves them into the structure as installed parts with the same quantity, origin and age; nothing is created or used up. After the final stability, binding, roof-load and runoff checks the shelter is commissioned: a 2 m x 1 m covered floor under a 1.2 m ridge and a roof sloping about 50 degrees. While exactly one person lies wholly on that floor in rain and wind up to 0.8, it removes up to 50% of the rain part and up to 35% of the wind part of the existing outdoor exposure chill, scaled by roof condition, by the share of the body under the roof along the wind-driven rain, and for wind by how directly the low edge faces the wind; wind entering the open side, stronger weather, water pooling on the floor or a second person gives no protection. Air temperature, hunger, nutrition and rest are unchanged, and copies never stack. A frame without its three roofing courses gives no rain protection. Each round installed parts wear by 0.0005 + 0.002 x rain + 0.002 x wind; a part below condition 0.5 makes a commissioned shelter unsafe with no protection until repair and a passing reinspection. Repair restores only the replaced parts; removed and dismantled parts return to the ground at the site with their condition and can be reused at that condition. Work not continued in a round pauses; a lost reserved material stops it. Cancel returns uninstalled materials once and leaves installed parts as an unfinished structure; death stops the work, drops uninstalled materials where the person died and leaves installed parts. No reward, mastery or refund.

candidates.costs: 2 energy per unit, finite current source stock.
candidates.effects: Transfers real source stock to inventory; requires the source interaction range. No processing or felling is implied.

candidates.effects: Requires actual distance within pickup reach; resource:ID means a matching nearby visible ground stack.

candidates.function: Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
candidates.costs: A game round to begin study after review; implementation time does not advance simulation.
candidates.effects: World review reuses equivalents or returns a structured development request. No request, learning or descriptive reward. Unknown methods and costs are allowed; the reviewer supplies a minimal feasible specification.

candidates.function: Portion and combine owned food you know as edible and nontoxic into one carried prepared stack by hand, without heat, water or equipment; resume or cancel unfinished work.
candidates.costs: Start: inputs lists 1-24 {itemId, quantity} allocations in 0.1 steps from exact owned, unreserved, unspoiled stacks of one food that your own record shows as edible with toxicity 0 (raw, or food already combined this way); preparation is cold-combine (default). Work equals the selected quantity: one food unit per round at one energy per unit worked, so 3 units take 3 rounds and 3 energy and a final partial unit costs its fraction. Start pays the first increment and the same action continues each round; resume pays the next increment of the unfinished process; cancel takes one round and no energy. No vessel, water, fuel or tool is needed or provided. Travel, gathering and eating are separate actions with their own costs.
candidates.effects: Start moves the selected quantities into a reserved in-progress portion that stays carried and owned, keeps its origin, age and decay, and keeps ageing. Completion replaces it with one portable prepared stack of the same food holding the same quantity and mass, with the original lots kept as separate component records. It eats exactly like that food through eat (same nutrition and toxicity per unit, the ordinary eat cost and satiety cap; a part eaten debits those lots), and each lot spoils under the existing rules without any shelf-life reset. No washing, cutting, heating, detoxification, preservation, digestibility change, extra nutrition, mastery or reward; preparing does not feed anyone. Work not continued in a round pauses with progress and ingredients kept; too little energy pauses without spending. A lost or spoiled reserved ingredient stops the work and returns the survivors. Cancel returns the remaining reserved food in its current condition; spent energy and time are never refunded. Death stops the work and leaves the unfinished food on the ground. Different foods cannot be combined in this version because no consistent per-portion mixture rule is represented; heated, wet or tool-based preparation is not implemented.

candidates.effects: Continues until within the target interaction area or a real failure. Empty target uses x/y. A resource:ID target selects only a remembered ground stack.

response.text: {"queries":[],"result_json":"{\"reviews\":[{\"actor\":\"sol\",\"decision\":\"develop\",\"ability\":null,\"reason\":\"The searched registry contains simple-shelter, but its contract explicitly permits protection for exactly one person and gives none with a second occupant. It does not cover a simultaneously shared shelter. Develop a general multi-bay assembly operation using its existing construction machinery, rather than claiming that machinery as new. Local material observations establish neither ownership nor suitability; construction cannot start from observations alone.\",\"specification\":\"Handoff: implement 'Assemble and maintain a multi-bay rain shelter', parameterized by site, orientation, exact material allocations, bay count and mode start/resume/cancel/inspect/repair/dismantle. Smallest shared version: two adjacent, independently braced lean-to bays, each with the existing 2 m x 2 m construction footprint and 2 m x 1 m covered resting floor, reached from the same unobstructed open side. Do not invent a spanning roof or remove structural members. Record code dependencies and reuse from simple-shelter, including staged assembly, provenance, roof checks, wear and exposure calculations; this is an occupancy/composition extension, not reinvention. Each bay requires 13 actual suitable branches, 4 actual suitable vines and 6 actual suitable bark units: two bays require 26, 8 and 12 respectively. Stone is not a substitute in this version. No tools are supplied or required for the existing hand-assembly method. Require reachable, clear, unoccupied, ordinary dry soil within world bounds, non-overlapping construction footprints, and an unobstructed approach wide enough for the actual users. Do not label the result universally accessible; its ridge remains 1.2 m, entry requires the actor's actual movement capabilities, and each occupant must fit wholly within one resting floor. No automatic travel, consent, construction help or occupancy for other actors. Use message for communication; each participant independently acts and pays their own applicable costs. Exact loose-source and inventory IDs must be supplied at execution; none are known for Sol's branches, bark or vines. Acquire through gather/pickup with their existing stock, distance and energy costs. Reuse probe for suitability observations or tests: one round and 0.2 energy for observation, or 0.5 energy and 0.1 real sample unit for a physical test. Testing consumes additional material, not the reserved whole construction units. No vines are currently established, so absent suitable real binding material construction pauses at the prerequisite, not at review. Study takes 4 rounds individually. Construction costs 12 one-round, one-energy increments per bay, 24 rounds and 24 energy for the two-bay version, excluding study, acquisition, travel and testing. Start pays only the first increment; energy shortages pause without charging an unperformed increment. Keep exact stage, bay, builder and material-lot progress. Reserved materials remain owned and age normally; each paid stage transfers only its listed parts into the structure without duplicating mass. Final checks commission each bay separately. A completed bay protects at most one fitting occupant; occupants in another bay must not disable this bay, but two in the same bay invalidate its protection. Apply the inherited maximum 50% rain-exposure-chill and 35% wind-exposure-chill reductions only for actual coverage, condition, orientation and wind no greater than 0.8; no shelter stacking, nutrition, air-temperature change or guaranteed rest bonus. Frames, failed checks, pooled floors and unsafe bays provide no protection. Protection tests consist of actual rain occupancy and outside/inside wetness or exposure observations; a paid wet probe can test a reachable sample or roof section but does not certify the whole shelter. Record weather and measured result, including leaks. Wear each installed part each world round by 0.0005 + 0.002*rain + 0.002*wind; condition below 0.5 disables the affected bay until replacement and passing reinspection. Inspect costs one round and 0.2 energy. Builder repair costs exact replacement parts for the selected inherited stage, one round and one energy; replaced parts remain real worn ground materials. Builder dismantling costs one round and one energy per stage and returns only installed parts at current condition. Interruption preserves partial work and reservations; resume pays the next stage after revalidation. Cancel costs one round, zero energy, releases unused reservations once and leaves installed work unfinished. Death stops work, drops unused carried material at death and leaves installed parts on site. No spent time or energy is refunded. Ongoing wear continues during ordinary simulation, not development waiting. Implement these validations and exposure rules in code, with no repeated model adjudication.\",\"learning\":4,\"experienceReview\":\"No benefit for requesting, naming, studying, registration or commissioning alone. Observable successful protection can produce personally applicable comfort, with total physical comfort capped at 10 and never reducing basic nutritional requirements. If the experience system supports it, actual protection during rain can give a short benefit capped at 1 per actor per 10 rounds; maintained satisfaction is capped at 1 for ongoing usable shelter access, refreshed only by actual use or maintenance and decaying at least 0.002 per round without qualifying activity. Functionally deduplicate across bays, shelter copies and equivalent comfort events. Genuine measured information gain, including a discovered leak or failed material test, may qualify once for that finding, not for repeated queries. Other users receive nothing unless they independently participate or experience the effect. Never modify protected rewards, budget, goals or permissions.\",\"visualReview\":\"Emit observable events for material installation, stage interruption, inspection results, commissioning, leaks, repair, occupancy and dismantling. Reusable visual metadata must include structure ID, bay IDs, footprint, orientation, open approach, installed-stage mask, roof coverage, per-bay condition, commissioning status and actual occupant positions. Render partial frames and missing roof courses accurately; show protected occupancy only when runtime coverage and weather checks pass. Failed construction or tests must not display completed shelter or successful protection.\"},{\"actor\":\"wren\",\"decision\":\"develop\",\"ability\":null,\"reason\":\"Searches found probe, consult and exchange but no planting or cultivation operation. Probe can inspect or test a sample, not place viable propagules in a maintained growing site. Food safety and 14 nutrition do not establish root viability or growing requirements. Develop a general planting-and-tending trial with an executable observation-only outcome when regeneration remains unsupported, not instant replenishment or a fictional guaranteed crop.\",\"specification\":\"Handoff: implement 'Establish and tend a cultivation trial', parameterized by visible plant/source reference, exact owned propagule lot and quantity, reachable ground site, and mode establish/tend/observe/resume/cancel/remove. Reuse probe and consult for their actual supported operations and record those dependencies; use the existing plant lifecycle and resource-transfer handlers where compatible, without claiming them as new. Initial applicable references are source start-0-roots at (10.1,12), observed stock 2 and capacity 6, and owned lot item-4-wren-46, quantity 3 with existing age and decay. Revalidate all at execution; neither source stock nor ownership is frozen by this review. The owned food's edibility is not evidence of a living crown, bud or seed. First inspect a real candidate and reachable ground using probe: observation costs one round and 0.2 energy; physical testing costs one round, 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit, preserving or consuming the sampled amount according to the performed test. Only observed evidence is reported. If no suitable living planting unit is established, leave the owned food untouched and allow a marked monitoring trial of the existing patch; do not invent a viable propagule. Minimal planting trial selects one actual whole viable unit, or a larger exact quantity when supported, and ground that can genuinely be loosened and covered by hand. No tool, water, fertilizer or seed is provided. Establishment has three one-round stages costing one energy each: prepare a small planting position appropriate to the actual propagule, place it, then cover and record. Site area, depth and suitability must come from observed propagule dimensions and applicable lifecycle requirements, not a universal guessed root depth. If the ground cannot be worked by hand, a real suitable tool or different workable site is required. Unplaced units remain reserved, owned and ageing; placement transfers the unit's quantity, provenance, mass and remaining viable state from inventory to the trial, not to food stock. Once planted it is unavailable to eat or plant elsewhere. Observation mode costs one round and 0.2 energy and records actual changes; tending costs one round and one energy per small trial plot, with an explicit supported action such as removing an observed competing plant by hand or restoring displaced soil. Irrigation requires actual accessible water, a feasible delivery method, exact quantity and paid collection/transport; it is not a free default action. Monitoring the existing patch need not remove its food or create a second plant. Runtime must bind to the real species' supported viability, moisture, light, soil, temperature and growth rules. Use the source's existing regeneration behavior if present; do not infer a rate from its stock/capacity or disclose hidden ecological parameters. If propagation is not yet modeled, implement establishment, environmental exposure, persistent trial records and comparison against the original patch as the feasible precursor, explicitly reporting that growth and yield are unverified. No autonomous food creation is enabled until a conserved, executable lifecycle is implemented in this same development handoff. Any enabled growth must advance only with elapsed simulation time and actual required environmental inputs; record growth inputs, viable biomass, stages, mortality and harvestable output. Never replenish by copying the planting unit or resetting the source. Harvest only observed mature stock through gather, debiting that stock at its existing costs. Preserve source food properties only where species identity remains established; nutrition is obtained through eating, not planting. Record elapsed rounds, placement stage, condition, observations and interventions. At 80 elapsed trial rounds offer an inconclusive status if no decisive change has occurred; this is an observation horizon, not a maturity deadline or unlock. Continued observation is optional. Real drought, waterlogging, decay, uprooting and inadequate conditions can stall or kill a trial. Growth and deterioration proceed during ordinary world simulation, not review waiting. Interruption preserves stage and reservations; resume rechecks site, energy and material validity and pays only subsequent work. Cancel costs one round and zero energy, releases unplaced survivors once, and leaves planted material in place. Removal costs one round and one energy and returns only the material actually recoverable in its current condition, never a guaranteed edible root. Death ends personal work, drops unplaced carried units and leaves the trial subject to ecology; independent actors may interact only through their own valid actions. Spent samples, labor and time are not refunded. Each learner studies individually for 2 rounds. Encode progress, accounting and failure rules rather than repeatedly asking a model to authorize growth.\",\"learning\":2,\"experienceReview\":\"Requests, study, marking a plot and merely scheduling observations grant nothing. A verified new finding about viability, sprouting, failure or environmental response can support one bounded information-gain benefit, capped at 1 per actor per 10 rounds and deduplicated by finding across probe and trial interfaces. Familiar genuine tending or successful harvesting may sustain modest satisfaction without requiring novelty: cap at 1, refresh only on personally performed meaningful care or real harvest, and decay at least 0.002 per round without qualifying activity. Do not reward empty observations or repeated ineffective tending. A failed trial can be informative but cannot count as successful production. Physical comfort remains capped at 10; eating real harvested food retains its full basic nutrition independent of mood. No protected reward, budget, goal or permission changes.\",\"visualReview\":\"Emit actual preparation, placement, tending, observation, emergence, wilting, death, removal and harvest events only when those events occur. Reusable metadata includes trial ID, source and lot references, site bounds, quantity placed, work stage, observation timestamps, measured condition, lifecycle stage and verified harvestable stock. Distinguish an observation marker from a planted unit and a planted unit from a sprout. Hidden roots remain visually hidden unless exposed by a real action. No lush crop, replenished stock, maturity indicator or successful-harvest animation may appear for an unverified, stalled or failed trial.\"}]}"}
